messages:
customer-jamie: Hey, started getting 401s a few hours after we switched our CLI credential helper. Worked earlier this morning. Error from API: {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid API key"}}

alex: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact curl you ran (sanitized token ok)?

customer-jamie: Sure: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer "sk_live_abcd1234..."" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","input":"hi"}'`

maria: Ah looks like the token is wrapped in quotes in the header (`Bearer "sk_..."`). That will be sent literally and fail with invalid_api_key.

alex: Can you check what the helper returns? `printf '%s\n' "$(your-helper get)" | od -c` — see if there are extra quote chars or escape sequences.

customer-jamie: Ran a quick check, helper prints `"sk_live_abcd1234..."` (with surrounding quotes). We use a credential-helper that stores JSON and returns the token field with quotes.

engops-ryan: Repro'd locally by storing a secret with literal quotes. Headers end up like `Authorization: Bearer "sk_..."` — the API treats that as wrong.

infra-jen: Quick fixes: 1) strip quotes when reading token in the script: `TOKEN=$(cat /path/to/token | sed -e 's/^"//' -e 's/"$//')` 2) fix credential helper config so it outputs raw token (no JSON quoting), or use `jq -r .token` against JSON output.

alex: If you pulled token into a k8s secret via Helm, check for `values.yaml` quoting. Helm chart `secret` values often keep quotes; use `|` block or `tpl` to avoid double quoting.

customer-jamie: Using `jq -r .api_key` fixed it for us. After updating the helper to raw output, calls started succeeding. Thanks! :tada:

maria: Filed a short KB entry for this class of failures (invalid_api_key when token contains literal quotes). Recommend adding a parse/validation step in the SDK to detect `^".*"$` and warn.

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0422 — root cause: credential-helper returned quoted token, produced malformed Authorization header -> 401 invalid_api_key.

alex: Leaving this thread open for a day to confirm no other teams hit it. If you want we can run a quick regex scan over recent support logs to find similar 401s with `"sk_` pattern.

customer-jamie: Sounds good, will ping if we see anything else. Thanks all :)
